subject: CometBank production: reserved-capacity shortfall causing spikes
messages:
From: Ahmed Salim <ahmed.salim@cometbank.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency spike / errors affecting customers

Hi Sean / Marissa,

We're seeing a significant degradation in our production traffic since ~07:40 PDT — 95th p99 latency for text generation jumped from ~120ms to ~900ms and our 5xx rate climbed to ~3% across several endpoints. This is impacting the fraud-decisions flow for a subset of customers (transactions failing at peak).

We are on your Dedicated plan (reserved GPU pool) and our monitoring indicates queueing / token throttling on your side. Can you confirm what's happening and timeline for mitigation? We need an ETA — this is customer-impacting and procurement may need to approve a burst if that's required.

Logs attached on our side (brief) — happy to jump on a call.

— Ahmed
Ops Lead, CometBank
attachments: comet_logs_20261020.txt (referenced)
From: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Ahmed Salim <ahmed.salim@cometbank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:29:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / errors affecting customers

Ahmed — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're on it.

Quick summary of immediate actions we're kicking off:
- Triage (Olga) will evaluate the Dedicated pool for noisy neighbors / reservation drift and look at queue depth & KV-cache hot keys.
- Short-term mitigation: shift a percentage of traffic to a quantized model-variant we host (lower GPU memory) + enable aggressive prefix caching for CometBank routes. This should reduce token compute and queueing.
- If headroom isn't sufficient, Marissa will work with procurement on a one-week emergency burst purchase while we fully remediate.

Olga — can you confirm whether we have burst capacity available now and whether the quantized variant can be routed without measurable business-impact? Also attaching internal capacity snapshot request: please add any diagnostic artifacts as attachments.

Ahmed — I'll keep you updated every 30-45 minutes until we have baseline restored.

— Sean
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ahmed Salim <ahmed.salim@cometbank.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / errors affecting customers

On Tue, Oct 20, 2026 at 08:29 AM sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com> wrote:
> Ahmed — thanks for the heads up and sorry for the disruption. We're on it.

I've pulled the Dedicated pool telemetry. Initial findings:
- Immediate cause: a combination of reservation drift (some hosts failed to pick up renewed reservations during a rolling maintenance window) and a noisy tenant with unusually long generation sequences (KV cache churn).
- Impact: per-host queue depth doubled, continuous batching latency increased, and we saw periodic token-timeouts that surface as 5xx.

Proposed mitigation (next 30–90 minutes):
1) Instant routing change: divert 25% of CometBank traffic to quantized model v2-q (compatible with eval set; expected quality delta <= 0.8% on PROMPT-100). This reduces per-token compute ~2.7x.
2) Enable route-specific prefix caching TTL bump (CometBank only) to reduce repeated context rebuilds.
3) If headroom still insufficient, apply emergency burst (we have spare capacity in region us-west-2 but it requires procurement approval to bill to the account).

Estimated improvements: expected 95th latency fall from ~900ms -> ~180–250ms within two batches post cutover; error rate should drop below 0.5%.

I've attached a capacity snapshot and KV cache diagnostics for your review. I'll implement step 1 now and report back with metrics.

attachments: capacity_snapshot_20261020.csv, kv_cache_diag.txt

— Olga
SRE, Serving Runtime
From: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Ahmed Salim <ahmed.salim@cometbank.com>, procurement@cometbank.com
Cc: sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / errors affecting customers

Ahmed — update below and a request: 

Status update:
- Olga routed 25% of traffic to v2-q and we started prefix caching for CometBank at 08:55 PDT. Initial telemetry shows p95 latency moving toward 200ms and 5xx waterfall clearing.
- We'll continue monitoring for 2 hours; full cutover can be expanded if behaviour is stable.

Request (procurement):
- To avoid further user impact we recommend a one-week emergency burst package (estimated cost: $27k) while we finish the remediation.
- CometBank procurement: please confirm approval or share a PO/DocuSign link. If needed, we can issue an invoice immediately and apply it against your reserved commitment.

Ask to Redwood leadership (Vivek cc'd):
- We may need a temporary credit/waiver on the burst charge depending on the post-mortem. Vivek, can you confirm whether you can authorize a partial credit pending final RCA?

I'll schedule a 30-minute sync at 11:00 PDT to review metrics and next steps.

Thanks — Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

To: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>, olga_petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Ahmed Salim <ahmed.salim@cometbank.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency spike / errors affecting customers

Marissa / team — thanks for the quick response and the clear remediation path.

Authorization: I approve an emergency burst for CometBank for up to one week to stabilize production. Work with Finance to generate a temporary invoice; I'll approve a conditional credit up to 50% of the burst cost pending closure of the RCA and demonstration of remediation (no repeat of reservation drift). DocuSign payment link (internal): https://docusign.example.com/inv/DEAL-7812-burst-approval

Operational asks:
- Olga: please complete a post-mortem focused on root cause (reservation lifecycle during maintenance) and include a remediation ticket with ETA for a permanent fix (no later than 2 business days).
- Sean / Marissa: present short incident readout to execs tomorrow at 10:00 AM (summary slide + remediation timeline).

Ahmed — I'm sorry for the disruption and appreciate the team working with you. We'll keep you looped and confirm when the credit is applied.

— Vivek
Chief Revenue Officer
Redwood Inference
